angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 520,036 km at 124.87 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.0085 +/- 0.0104 mas (same row, RUWE 0.82): 124.87 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.7475 +/- 0.0077 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-78 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 520,036 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.779 +/- 0.032 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-78 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5058 +/- 50 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-78 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-78 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-78.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.582, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-78 (pscomppars): spectral type G, from Sanchis-Ojeda et al. 2013 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...774...54S/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-78 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.18 dex, from Bonomo et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-78 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.49785, from Iglesias-Marzoa et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015PASP..127..567I/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-78 (pscomppars): age 0.625 Gyr, from Grunblatt et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...808..127G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-78 (pscomppars): rotation period 12.92 d, from Bonomo et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
